kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Parthian or Middle Persian 𐭮𐭭𐭣𐭥𐭮 (sndws, “a silk (or brocade) garment”), from Sogdian [script needed] (sndws /⁠sandus⁠/, “a silk wear”), compare also Old Armenian սնդուս (sndus) an Iranian loanword. From an Anatolian source, compare Ancient Greek σάνδυξ (sándux, “a Lydian red fabric”), likely ultimately descendant from Akkadian 𒉌𒌓𒍝𒄢 (NA₄.GUG /⁠sāmtu, sāntu, sāndu⁠/, “red stone, carnelian, cinnabar”).
s: Middle Persian 𐭮𐭭𐭣𐭥𐭮 (sndws, “a silk (or brocade) garment”)
Ancient Greek σάνδυξ (sándux, “a Lydian red fabric”)
Akkadian 𒉌𒌓𒍝𒄢 (NA₄.GUG /⁠sāmtu, sāntu, sāndu⁠/, “red stone, carnelian, cinnabar”)
